tour: PC1, PC2 and PC3 explain 59%, 18% and 10% of the variance across 759 drugs. PC1 is driven mostly by acceptors and weight, PC2 by aromatic rings and Fsp3, PC3 by log P and Fsp3. Colours mark the three largest ATC groups.
In this map 53% of 759 drugs have a nearest neighbour from the same ATC anatomical group, against 33% in the descriptor space of step 1 and 13% by chance.

Among the 708 drugs up to 1000 Da, log P runs from −8.2 (Streptomycin) to 9.8 (Temoporfin); the median is 2.6. 81 (11%) are above 5, Lipinski's limit. The 51 larger drugs, mostly peptides, are left out from here on: Crippen log P falls as low as −43 for them, and Hansch analysis is about small molecules. Depth is random spread so the points do not overlap.

Among the 599 drugs up to 500 Da, Pearson r between log P and MR is 0.61: larger small molecules tend to be greasier. Across all 759 it is −0.69, because peptides and other large polar drugs have a high MR and a very low log P.
91% of the 531 drugs with an oral route sit at or below 140 Å², against 70% of the 158 drugs given only by other routes.
308 of 759 drugs have a value. Median pChEMBL 7.9 (interquartile range 6.9 to 8.6), about 12 nM.

These 8 drugs share CHEMBL233 (Mu opioid receptor antagonist) as their first mechanism target. Of the 3 models allowed at this size (one descriptor per five drugs), log P gave the best leave-one-out q².
Pool all 299 drugs with an activity value, whatever their target, and the best model is log P + MR + TPSA with r² = 0.15 and q² = 0.13.
tourEq:
pChEMBL = 7.704 (±0.269) + 0.304 (±0.087) log P
r² 0.67 · q² 0.42 · s 0.32 · n 8
Weak. q² is 0.42: better than the mean, but below the usual 0.5 bar, and 4 of 100 shuffled fits matched its r².

pChEMBL = 6.464 (±0.220) − 0.012 (±0.063) log P + 0.017 (±0.0038) MR − 0.0062 (±0.0026) TPSA
Not predictive. q² is 0.13, close to zero.
boot.seriesTail: The surface is the fitted equation. Each thin line joins a drug to the surface, so its length is the residual.
